265.subject: Botany
265.text: The family containing mustard and its main characters are
options: Brassicaceae - Tetramerous flowers, six stamens, bicarpellary gynoecium, siliqua type fruit
Brassicaceae - Pentamerous flowers, many stamens, pentacarpellary gynoecium, capsule type fruit
Solanaceae - Pentamerous flowers, five stamens, bicarpellary gynoecium, berry type fruit
Poaceae - Trimerous flowers, three stamens, monocarpellary gynoecium, caryopsis type of fruit.
265.sol: Brassica (mustard) belongs to family Brassicaceae. Family brassicaceae is characterised by polypetalous 4 petals, polysepalous 4 sepals, six stamens (which are in tetradynamous condition i.e. 4 +2 or in two whorls, 4 inner long and 2 outer short). Gynoecium is bicarpellary, syncarpous unilocular with parietal placentation. Fruit is usually siliqua (dry dehiscent fruit formed by bicarpellary syncarpous gynoecium with replum) and rarely lomentum.

772.text: The standard half-cell reduction potential for $\mathrm{Ag}^{+} \mid \mathrm{Ag}$ is $0.7991 \mathrm{~V}$ at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Given the experimental value $K_{s p}=1.56 \times 10^{-10}$ for $\mathrm{AgCl}$, calculate the standard half-cell reduction potential for the $\mathrm{Ag} \mid \mathrm{AgCl}$ electrode.
772.sol:
For the desired reaction,

$\mathrm{AgCl}+$1 e^{-} $\rightarrow \mathrm{Ag}+\mathrm{Cl}^{-}, \quad$E^{{}^{\circ}}=$\frac{-\Delta_r G^{{}^{\circ}}}{(1) F}$The needed $\Delta_r G^{{}^{\circ}}$ can be obtained by adding the values of $\Delta_r G^{{}^{\circ}}$ for the reactions

$\begin{aligned}$& $\mathrm{Ag}^{+}+$1 e^{-} $\rightarrow \mathrm{Ag}$; $\Delta$G^{{}^{\circ}}=-n F E^{{}^{\circ}} \\
& $\mathrm{AgCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{Ag}^{+}+\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$; $\Delta$G^{{}^{\circ}}=-R T \ln K_{s p}, $\text{ giving }$\\
& \Delta_r G^{{}^{\circ}}=-(1 $\mathrm{~mol})\left($9.648 $\times$10^4 $\mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~mol}{ }^{-1} \mathrm{~V}^{-1}\right)($0.7991 $\mathrm{~V})$\\
& \quad-$\left($8.314 $\mathrm{JK}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right)($298 $\mathrm{~K}) \ln \left($1.56 $\times$10^{-10}\right) \\
& =-77.10 $\mathrm{~kJ}+$55.95 $\mathrm{~kJ}=-$21.15 $\mathrm{~kJ}
\end{aligned}$The potential is $E^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{-(-21.15)}{(1)(96.485)}=+0.2192 \mathrm{~V}$.

3531.subject: Chemistry
3531.text: Which among the following is colored?
3531.sol:
$CuCl$ has the copper in $+ 1$ oxidation state. It has the ten electrons in d-orbital. All the electrons are paired. So, it is not coloured.

${ScCl}_{3}$ has the ${Sc}^{3 +}$. It has the $d^{0}$ configuration. It has all paired electrons. So, it has no colour.

${CuCl}_{2}$ has the ${Cu}^{2 +}$. It has the $d^{9}$ configuration. So, it has the unpaired electron. So, it can show the colour due to $d - d$ transition by the unpaired electron. So, it is coloured compound.

${TiCl}_{4}$ has the ${Ti}^{4 +}$. It has the $d^{0}$ configuration. It has all paired electrons. So, it has no colour.

Hence, the ${CuCl}_{2}$ is coloured.

6210.text: If $g ( x ) = \dfrac{1}{6}f\left(3x^{2} - 1\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}f\left(1 - x^{2}\right), ∀ x \in \mathbb{R}$, where $f^{''} ( x ) > 0, ∀ x \in \mathbb{R}$. Then $g ( x )$& is increasing in the interval
6210.sol:
$g\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{6}f\left(3{x}^{2} - 1\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}f\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)$

$⇒ {g}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{6}{f}^{'}\left(3{x}^{2} - 1\right) \cdot 6x + \dfrac{1}{2}{f}^{'}\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right) \cdot \left(- 2x\right)$

$⇒ {g}^{'}\left(x\right) = x\left[{f}^{'}\left(3{x}^{2} - 1\right) - {f}^{'}\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)\right]$

For $g ( x )$ to be increasing function

$⇒ {g}^{'}\left(x\right) = x\left[{f}^{'}\left(3{x}^{2} - 1\right) - {f}^{'}\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)\right] > 0$

$\text{So,if}x > 0$

$⇒ \left[{f}^{'}\left(3{x}^{2} - 1\right) - {f}^{'}\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)\right] > 0$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(3{x}^{2} - 1\right) > {f}^{'}\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)$

$⇒ \left(3{x}^{2} - 1\right) > \left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)$

$⇒ 4{x}^{2} > 2$

$⇒ {x}^{2} > \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ x \in \left(\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{2}}, \infty\right)$

$\text{if}x < 0$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(3{x}^{2} - 1\right) < {f}^{'}\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)$

$⇒ \left(3{x}^{2} - 1\right) < \left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)$

$⇒ {x}^{2} < \dfrac{1}{2} \text{ and } x < 0 ⇒ x \in \left(- \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, 0\right)$

$⇒ g ( x ) \text{increasing in}\left(- \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{2}}, 0\right) ∪ \left(\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{2}}, \infty\right)$

6333.text: The volume of sphere is increasing at the rate of 1200 $\mathrm{cu} \mathrm{cm} / \mathrm{s}$. The rate of increase in its surface area when the radius is $10 \mathrm{ cm}$ is
6333.sol:
Let $V$ be the volume, $S$ be the surface area and $r$ be the radius of the sphere.
It is given that, $\frac{d V}{d t}=1200 \mathrm{cu} \mathrm{cm} / \mathrm{s} and r=10 \mathrm{ cm}$
Now, Volume of sphere $=V=\frac{4}{3} \pi r^3\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad \frac{d V}{d t}=\frac{4}{3} \pi 3 r^2 \frac{d r}{d t} \\
& 1200=4 \pi(10)^2 \frac{d r}{d t} \\
& \frac{d r}{d t}=\frac{3}{\pi}
\end{aligned}$
and Surface Area of sphere,
$\begin{aligned}
& S=4 \pi r^2=\frac{d S}{d t}=4 \pi \cdot 2 r \frac{d r}{d t} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d S}{d t}=4 \pi \cdot 2(10) \frac{d r}{d t} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d S}{d t}=4 \pi \cdot 2 \times 10\left(\frac{3}{\pi}\right) \\
& \therefore \quad \frac{d S}{d t}=240 \mathrm{sq} \mathrm{cm} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}$

12474.text: The harmonic conjugate of $(2,3,4)$ with respect to the points $(3,-2,2)$ and $(6,-17,-4)$ is
12474.sol:
Let $A=(3,-2,2) \begin{aligned}$& B=(6,-17,-4) \\
& P=(2,3,4)
\end{aligned}

Let $P$ divides $A B$ in the ratio of $m: n$.

$\begin{gathered}$P=$\left[\frac{m x_2+n x_1}{m+n}, \frac{m y_2+n y_1}{m+n}, \frac{m z_2+n z_1}{m+n}\right]$\\
(2,3,4)=$\left[\frac{m(6)+n(3)}{m+n}, \frac{m(-17)+n(-2)}{m+n},\right.$\\
(2,3,4)=$\left[\frac{6 m(-4)+n(2)}{m+n}\right]$\\
$\frac{6 m+3 n}{m+n}=$2 \\
6 m+3 n=2 m+2 n \\
4 m=-n \\
$\frac{m}{n}=-\frac{1}{4}$\\
m: n=-1: 4
\end{gathered}

We know that,
If point $P$ divides a line segment in the ratio of $m: n$, then its harmonic conjugate will divide same segment in the ratio of $-m: n\therefore$ Required ratio $=-m: n=1: 4\therefore$ Required harmonic conjugate

$\begin{aligned}$& =$\left(\frac{m x_2+n x_1}{m+n}, \frac{m y_2+n y_1}{m+n}, \frac{m z_2+n z_1}{m+n}\right)$\\
& =$\left(\frac{1(6)+4(3)}{1+4}, \frac{1(-17)+4(-2)}{1+4}, \frac{1(-4)+4(2)}{1+4}\right)$\\
& =$\left(\frac{18}{5}, \frac{-25}{5}, \frac{4}{5}\right)=\left(\frac{18}{5},-$5, $\frac{4}{5}\right)
\end{aligned}$Hence option (4) is correct.

17387.text:
If for a first order reaction, the value of $A$ and $E_a$ are $4 \times 10^{13} \mathrm{ s}^{-1}$ and $98.6 \mathrm{ kJ} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$
respectively, then at what temperature will its half life period be 10 minutes?
17387.sol:
According to Arrhenius equation,
$\log k=\log A-\frac{E_a}{2.303 R T}...(i)$
For $1^{\text{st }}$ order reaction,
$k=\frac{0.693}{t_{1 / 2}}=\frac{0.693}{600 s}=1.1 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{ s}^{-1}$
Substitute the value of $k$ in Eq. (i)
$\log \left(1.1 \times 10^{-3}\right)=\log \left(4 \times 10^{13}\right)-\frac{98.6 \times 10^3}{2.303 \times 8.314 \times T}$
Solving for $T$,
$T=311.15 \mathrm{ K}$

18837.text: A neutron moving with speed v makes a head on collision with a hydrogen atom in ground state kept at rest. The minimum kinetic energy of the neutron for which inelastic collision takes place is
18837.sol: Let speed of neutron before collision $=\mathrm{V}$ Speed of neutron after collision $=\mathrm{V}_{1}$ Speed of proton or hydrogen atom after collision $=\mathrm{V}_{2}$ Energy of excitation $=\Delta \mathrm{E}$ From the law of conservation of linear momentum, $\mathrm{mv}=\mathrm{mv}_{1}+\mathrm{mv}_{2}$ And for law of conservation of energy, $\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^{2}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{1}^{2}+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{2}^{2}$ From squaring eq. (i), we get v^{2}=v_{1}^{2}+v_{2}^{2}+2 v_{1} v_{2} From squaring eq. (ii), we get v^{2}=v_{1}^{2}+v_{2}^{2}+$\frac{2 \Delta E}{m}$ From eqn (3) \& (4) $\begin{aligned} \therefore2 \mathrm{v}_{1} \mathrm{v}_{2}&=\frac{2 \Delta \mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{m}}\\ \therefore\left(\mathrm{v}_{1}-\mathrm{v}_{2}\right)^{2}&=\left(\mathrm{v}_{1}+\mathrm{v}_{2}\right)^{2}-4 \mathrm{v}_{1} \mathrm{v}_{2}=\mathrmv^{2}-\frac{4 \Delta \mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{m}} \end{aligned}$ As, $v_{1}-v_{2}$ must be real, $v^{2}-\frac{4 \Delta E}{m} \geq 0$ \Rightarrow \quad $\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^{2} \geq2 $\Delta $\mathrm{E}$ The minimum energy that can be absorbed by the hydrogen atom in the ground state to go into the excited state is $10.2 \mathrm{eV}$. Therefore, the maximum kinetic energy needed is $\frac{1}{2}$ m v_{\min }^{2}=2 $\times10.2=20.4 \mathrm{eV}$

What is the order of reaction with respect to decomposition of XY?
19891.sol:
The rate law for the decomposition of XY is given by $Rate = k[XY]^{n}$, where $n$ is the order of the reaction.

Using the data from the table:
For $[XY]_1 = 0.4$ mol/L, $Rate_1 = 5.5 \times 10^{-7}$ mol/L s.

Taking the ratio of the rates:
$\dfrac{Rate_2}{Rate_1} = \left( \dfrac{[XY]_2}{[XY]_1} \right)^{n}$

$\dfrac{22.0 \times 10^{-7}}{5.5 \times 10^{-7}} = \left( \dfrac{0.8}{0.4} \right)^{n}$

$4 = 2^{n}$

Since $4 = 2^{2}$, we have $n = 2$.

Verifying with the third data point:
For $[XY]_3 = 1.2$ mol/L, $Rate_3 = 49.5 \times 10^{-7}$ mol/L s.
$\dfrac{Rate_3}{Rate_1} = \left( \dfrac{1.2}{0.4} \right)^{2} = 3^{2} = 9$.
$\dfrac{49.5 \times 10^{-7}}{5.5 \times 10^{-7}} = 9$.

The order of the reaction is 2.

Answer: 2

19986.subject: Chemistry
19986.text: Choose the coordination compound which does not exhibit Optical activity.
19986.sol:
Optical activity in coordination compounds requires the absence of a plane of symmetry and a center of inversion.

The complex $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_3\right]^{3+}$ is a tris-chelated octahedral complex which lacks both a plane of symmetry and a center of inversion, hence it is optically active.

The complex cis $-\left[\mathrm{CoCl}_2(\mathrm{en}$)_2\right]^{+} lacks a plane$ of symmetry and a center of inversion, making it optically active.

The complex cis-\left[\mathrm{PtCl}_2(\mathrm{en})_2\right]^{2+}$ also lacks a plane of symmetry and a center of inversion, making it optically active.

The complex trans $-\left[\mathrm{CoCl}_2(\mathrm{en})_2\right]^{+} possesses a plane$ of symmetry (the equatorial plane containing the metal and the two chlorine atoms) and a center of inversion. Therefore, it is achiral and does not exhibit optical activity.

Answer: trans-$\left[\mathrm{CoCl}_2(\mathrm{en})_2\right]^{+}$

20389.subject: Chemistry
20389.text: The correct order of reactivity of halogens with alkanes is:
20389.sol:
The reactivity of halogens towards alkanes is determined by the bond dissociation energy of the halogen molecule and the enthalpy of the reaction. The reaction of an alkane with a halogen is represented as $R-H + X_2 \rightarrow R-X + H-X$.

The reactivity order is governed by the strength of the $H-X$ bond formed and the ease of breaking the $X-X$ bond. Fluorine is the most reactive due to its high electronegativity and the high bond energy of the $H-F$ bond formed, which makes the reaction highly exothermic. Iodine is the least reactive because the reaction is endothermic and the $H-I$ bond is relatively weak.

The experimental order of reactivity for halogens with alkanes is $F_2 > Cl_2 > Br_2 > I_2$.

Answer: $F_2 > C l_2 > B r_2 > I_2$

21320.subject: Mathematics
21320.text: Find the particular solution of the differential equation $x^2 d y=\left(2 x y+y^2\right) d x$ given that $y=1$ when $x=1$
21320.sol:
The given differential equation is $x^{2} dy = (2xy + y^{2}) dx$, which can be written as $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2xy + y^{2}}{x^{2}}$.

This is a homogeneous differential equation. Let $y = vx$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x \dfrac{dv}{dx}$.

Substituting these into the equation: $v + x \dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{2x(vx) + (vx)^{2}}{x^{2}} = \dfrac{2vx^{2} + v^{2}x^{2}}{x^{2}} = 2v + v^{2}$.

Rearranging the terms: $x \dfrac{dv}{dx} = 2v + v^{2} - v = v^{2} + v$.

Separating the variables: $\dfrac{dv}{v^{2} + v} = \dfrac{dx}{x}$, which is $\dfrac{dv}{v(v+1)} = \dfrac{dx}{x}$.

Using partial fractions: $\left( \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{v+1} \right) dv = \dfrac{dx}{x}$.

Integrating both sides: $\ln|v| - \ln|v+1| = \ln|x| + C$, which simplifies to $\ln \left| \dfrac{v}{v+1} \right| = \ln|x| + C$.

Exponentiating: $\dfrac{v}{v+1} = Cx$.

Substituting $v = \dfrac{y}{x}$: $\dfrac{y/x}{y/x + 1} = Cx \Rightarrow \dfrac{y}{y+x} = Cx \Rightarrow y = Cx(y+x)$.

Given $y=1$ when $x=1$: $1 = C(1)(1+1) \Rightarrow 1 = 2C \Rightarrow C = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Substituting $C = \dfrac{1}{2}$ into the equation: $y = \dfrac{1}{2}x(y+x) \Rightarrow 2y = x(x+y)$.

Answer: $2 y=x(x+y)$

22225.text: If $\sin 3 \theta=\sin \theta$, how many solutions exist such that $-2 \pi < \theta < 2 \pi$ ?
22225.sol:
We have,

$\begin{aligned}&\Rightarrow \quad \sin 3 \theta=\sin \theta\\
&\Rightarrow \quad \quad 3 \sin \theta-4 \sin ^{3} \theta=\sin \theta\\
&\Rightarrow \quad \quad 4 \sin ^{3} \theta-2 \sin \theta=0 \\
&\Rightarrow \quad 2 \sin \theta\left(2 \sin ^{2} \theta-1\right)=0 \\
&\Rightarrow \quad \sin \theta=0 \text{$ or $} \sin \theta=\pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\\
&\text{ If } \sin \theta=0 \text{ and if } \sin \theta=\pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\\
&\Rightarrow \quad \theta=0, \pi,-\pi\\
&\Rightarrow \quad \theta, \frac{3 \pi}{4}, \frac{-5 \pi}{4}, \frac{-7 \pi}{4}, \frac{-\pi}{4}, \frac{-3 \pi}{4}, \frac{5 \pi}{4}, \frac{7 \pi}{4}
\end{aligned}\therefore$ There are nine solutions.

22622.subject: Physics
22622.text: The resistance of a wire is $R$ ohm. If it is melted and stretched to $n$ times its original length, its new resistance will be
22622.sol:
The resistance of a wire is given by $R = \rho \dfrac{l}{A}$, where $\rho$ is the resistivity, $l$ is the length, and $A$ is the cross-sectional area.

When the wire is stretched to $n$ times its original length, the new length becomes $l' = nl$. Since the volume of the wire remains constant during stretching, $V = A \times l = A' \times l'$.

Substituting $l' = nl$, we get $A \times l = A' \times nl$, which implies $A' = \dfrac{A}{n}$.

The new resistance $R'$ is given by $R' = \rho \dfrac{l'}{A'}$.

Substituting the values of $l'$ and $A'$, we get $R' = \rho \dfrac{nl}{A/n} = n^{2} \rho \dfrac{l}{A}$.

Since $R = \rho \dfrac{l}{A}$, it follows that $R' = n^{2} R$.

Answer: $n^{2} R$

23167.text: The stress verses strain graph of four metals A,B,C and D are as shown. Which of the graph represent the metal having greatest Young's modulus?
23167.sol:
The Young's modulus $Y$ of a material is defined as the ratio of stress to strain within the elastic limit, which corresponds to the slope of the stress-strain graph.

$Y = \dfrac{\text{stress}}{\text{strain}} = \tan(\theta)$

where $\theta$ is the angle that the stress-strain line makes with the strain axis.

Comparing the slopes of the given lines OA, OB, OC, and OD, the line OA makes the largest angle with the strain axis. Therefore, the slope of line OA is the greatest.

Since the slope represents the Young's modulus, the metal represented by graph OA has the greatest Young's modulus.

Answer: Graph OA

23358.subject: Physics
23358.text: One surface of a lens is convex and the other is concave. If the radii of curvatures are $R$ and $r$ respectively, the lens will be convex if
23358.sol:
The lens maker formula is given by $\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right).

For a lens$ with one convex surface and one concave surface, let the radius of the convex surface beR_1 = R$ and the radius of the concave surface be $R_2 = r$. By sign convention, for a convex surface facing the object, $R_1$ is positive, and for a concave surface, $R_2$ is also positive if the center of curvature lies on the same side as the light direction.

The focal length $f$ is given by \dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu -$1) $\left( \dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{r} \right)$.

For the lens to be convex (converging), the focal length $f$ must be positive. This requires $\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{r} \gt 0$.

Rearranging the inequality, $\dfrac{1}{R} \gt \dfrac{1}{r}$, which implies $R \lt r$.

Answer: $R \lt r$

CASE 1:

For $x \le - 2,$

25373.text: Let $f: \left(0, 1\right) \to \mathbb{R}$ be the function defined as $f\left(x\right) = \left[4x\right]{\left(x - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2}\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$, where $[ x ]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$. Then which of the following is(are) true?
options: The function $f$ is discontinuous exactly at one point in $( 0, 1 )$
There is exactly one point in $( 0, 1 )$ at which the function $f$ is continuous but NOT differentiable
The function $f$ is NOT differentiable at more than three points in $( 0, 1 )$
The minimum value of the function $f$ is $- \dfrac{1}{512}$
25373.sol:
Given,

$f: ( 0, 1 ) \to \mathbb{R}$

$f\left(x\right) = \left[4x\right]{\left(x - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2}\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

We know that, $\left[4x\right]$ will be discontinuous function at integer points,

So, $\text{critical point} = \dfrac{1}{4}, \dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{3}{4}$ as $x \in \left(0, 1\right)$

And function will be discontinuous at $x = \dfrac{3}{4}$ because for $\dfrac{1}{2} \text{ and } \dfrac{1}{4}$, $\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) \text{ and } {\left(x - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2}$ will make the function continuos

Hence, the function is discontinuous exactly at one point in $\left(0, 1\right)$, so option $\left(A\right)$ is correct,

Now,

$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}0, 0 < x < \dfrac{1}{4} \\ 1 \cdot {\left(x - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2}\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right), \dfrac{1}{4} \le x < \dfrac{1}{2} \\ 2 \cdot {\left(x - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2}\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right), \dfrac{1}{2} \le x < \dfrac{3}{4} \\ 3 \cdot {\left(x - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2}\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right), \dfrac{3}{4} \le x < 1\end{array}\right)

Now differentiating the above function we get,

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}0, 0 < x < \dfrac{1}{4} \\ {\left(x - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2} + 2\left(x - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right), \dfrac{1}{4} \le x < \dfrac{1}{2} \\ 4 \cdot \left(x - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) + 2{\left(x - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2}, \dfrac{1}{2} \le x < \dfrac{3}{4} \\ 3 \cdot {\left(x - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2} + 6\left(x - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right), \dfrac{3}{4} \le x < 1\end{array}\right)

Now from above function we get,

${f}^{'}\left(\dfrac{1}{4} -\right) = {f}^{'}\left(\dfrac{1}{4} +\right) = 0$ so function is differentiable at $x = \dfrac{1}{4}$

And ${f}^{'}\left(\dfrac{1}{2} -\right) = \dfrac{1}{16} \text{ and } {f}^{'}\left(\dfrac{1}{2} +\right) = 2 \times \dfrac{1}{16} = \dfrac{1}{8}$ so function is non-differentiable at $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$, hence option $\left(B\right)$ is correct,

Now ${f}^{'}\left(\dfrac{3}{4} -\right) = 4 \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{4} + 2 \times \dfrac{1}{4} = 1 \text{ and } {f}^{'}\left(\dfrac{3}{4} +\right) = 3 \times \dfrac{1}{4} + 6 \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Hence, the function is not differentiable at $x = \dfrac{3}{4}$

So, function non-differentiable at two points so option $\left(C\right)$ is not correct.

Now plotting the graph from the above value we get,

Now $f\left(x\right)$ will be minimum between $\dfrac{1}{4} \le x < \dfrac{1}{2}$

So, $f\left(x\right) = {\left(x - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2}\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right), \dfrac{1}{4} \le x < \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = {\left(x - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2} + 2\left(x - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \left(x - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)\left(3x - \dfrac{5}{4}\right)$

Now critical points will be ${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 0 ⇒ x = \dfrac{1}{4}\text{or}x = \dfrac{5}{12}$

Now putting the value in first derivative we get,

${f}^{'}\left(\dfrac{5}{12} -\right) 0$

Hence, $x = \dfrac{5}{12}$ is point of minima,

So, $f{\left(\dfrac{5}{12}\right)}_{min} = {\left(\dfrac{5}{12} - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2}\left(\dfrac{5}{12} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{- 1}{432}$

Hence, option $\left(D\right)$ is wrong.

26200.text: A thin spherical insulating shell of radius $R$ carries a uniformly distributed charge such that the potential at its surface is ${V}_{0}$ . A hole with a small area $\alpha4\pi{R}^{2}\left(\alpha ≪ 1\right)$ is made on the shell without affecting the rest of the shell. Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: The magnitude of electric field at the center of the shell is reduced by  $\dfrac{\alpha{V}_{0}}{2R}$
The potential at the center of the shell is reduced by  $2\alpha{V}_{0}$
The ratio of the potential at the center of the shell to that of the point at  $\dfrac{1}{2}R$  from center towards the hole will be  $\dfrac{1 - \alpha}{1 - 2\alpha}$

The magnitude of electric field at a point, located on a line passing through the hole and shell's center on a distance  $2R$  from the center of the spherical shell will be reduced by  $\dfrac{\alpha{V}_{0}}{2R}$
26200.sol:
Let $‘A’$ be the point at a distance $2R$ from center and $‘B’$ be the point at a distance of $\dfrac{R}{2}$ from center.
Now, let total charge on spherical shell distributed uniformly $= Q$
$⇒ Chargeperunitarea = \dfrac{Q}{4\pi{r}^{2}}$
Charge on elemental area $‘dA’$ .
Given potential at surface ${= V}_{0}$
$⇒ {V}_{0} = \dfrac{KQ}{R}$
Now, potential at center of the shell ${= V}_{C}$
${V}_{C} = \dfrac{KQ}{R} - \dfrac{K ( dQ )}{R} = \dfrac{KQ}{R} - \dfrac{K ( \alphaQ )}{R} = \dfrac{KQ}{R} ( 1 - \alpha )$
$⇒ {V}_{C} = {V}_{0}\left(1 - \alpha\right) ⇒ \text{Reduced}by\alpha{V}_{0}$
Now potential $= {V}_{B}$
$⇒ {V}_{B} = \dfrac{KQ}{R} - \dfrac{K\left(aQ\right)}{R / 2} = {V}_{0}\left(1 - 2a\right) ⇒ Reducedby2\alpha{V}_{0}$
$∴ \dfrac{{V}_{C}}{{V}_{B}} = \dfrac{1 - a}{1 - 2a}$
Now, electric field at $A = {E}_{A}$
Then, ${E}_{A} = \dfrac{KQ}{{\left(2R\right)}^{2}} - \dfrac{KaQ}{{R}^{2}} = \dfrac{KQ}{4{R}^{2}} - \dfrac{a{V}_{0}}{R}$
So reduced by $\dfrac{a{V}_{0}}{R}$
Electric field at center $‘C’$ due to small change $‘dQ’$
${E}_{C} = \dfrac{K\left(dq\right)}{{R}^{2}} = \dfrac{K\left(\alphaQ\right)}{{R}^{2}} = \dfrac{\alpha{V}_{0}}{R}$
So increased by $\dfrac{a{V}_{0}}{R}$

26714.text: In a particular system of units, a physical quantity can be expressed in terms of the electric charge $e$, electron mass ${m}_{e}$. Planck's constant $h$, and Coulomb's constant $k = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}$, where ${ε}_{0}$ is the permittivity of vacuum. In terms of these physical constants, the dimension of the magnetic field is $\left[B\right] = {\left[e\right]}^{\alpha}{\left[{m}_{e}\right]}^{\beta}{\left[h\right]}^{\gamma}{\left[k\right]}^{\delta}$. The value of $\alpha + \beta + \gamma + \delta$ is _______.
26714.sol:
Given here: $\left[B\right] = {\left[e\right]}^{\alpha}{\left[{m}_{e}\right]}^{\beta}{\left[h\right]}^{\gamma}{\left[k\right]}^{\delta}$

The dimensions of $\left[e\right] = \left[Current \times time\right] = \left[IT\right] and \left[{m}_{e}\right] = \left[M\right]$, Planck's constant $\left[h\right] = \dfrac{Energy}{Frequency} = \dfrac{\left[M{L}^{2}{T}^{- 2}\right]}{\left[{T}^{- 1}\right]} = \left[M{L}^{2}{T}^{- 1}\right]$ and $\left[k\right] = \dfrac{1}{\left[{ε}_{0}\right]$} = {$\left[{M}^{- 1}{L}^{- 3}{T}^{4}{I}^{2}\right]}^{- 1} = \left[M{L}^{3}{T}^{- 4}{I}^{- 2}\right]

Using Principle$ of $homogeneity,

\left[{M}^{1}{T}^{- 2}{I}^{- 1}\right] = {\left[IT\right]}^{\alpha}{\left[M\right]}^{\beta}{\left[M{L}^{2}{T}^{- 1}\right]}^{\gamma}{\left[M{L}^{3}{T}^{- 4}{I}^{- 2}\right]}^{\delta}$

Comparing both sides, we get

$\beta + \gamma + \delta = 1 . . . \left(i\right)

$2\gamma + 3\delta = 0 . . . $\left(ii\right)$

$\alpha - \gamma - 4\delta = - 2 . . . \left(iii\right)

$\alpha - 2\delta = - 1 . . . $\left(iv\right)$

On solving above four equations, we get

$\alpha = 3, \beta = - 4, \gamma = 3$ and $\delta = 2$

So, $\alpha + \beta + \gamma + \delta = 4$

28476.subject: Chemistry
28476.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
28476.text: The correct trend in the first ionization enthalpies of the elements in the $3^{\text{rd }}$ period of periodic table is :
28476.sol:
First ionization enthalpy generally increases across a period due to increasing nuclear charge and decreasing atomic radius. However, exceptions occur based on electron configuration stability.
For 3rd period elements, the approximate ionization enthalpy values are: Al (578), Si (787), P (1012), S (1000), Cl (1251) kJ/mol.
(1) Al has lower IE than Si because removing 3p¹ is easier than removing one electron from 3p².
(2) S has slightly lower IE than P despite being to the right because P has a half-filled p-orbital (3p³) which is more stable.
(3) Cl has the highest IE as it approaches a filled p-orbital.
The correct order is: Al < Si < S < P < Cl

29153.text: The spin-only magnetic moment value of the compound with strongest oxidizing ability among ${MnF}_{4}, {MnF}_{3}$ and ${MnF}_{2}$ is_____ $B . M$ (nearest integer)
29153.sol:
The change from Mn3+ to Mn2+ results in the half-filled (d5 ) configuration which has extra stability.So, MnF3 has most oxidising tendency.

Hence, ${MnF}_{3}$ has the strongest oxidizing ability as it undergoes reduction readily.

Spin only magnetic moment is calculated using the following formula

$\mu = \sqrt{n\left(n + 2\right)}B . M$

$\mu = \sqrt{4\left(4 + 2\right)} = \sqrt{24} = 4 . 89 = 5B . M$

29632.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : A mixture of C$_{12}$H$_{22}$O$_{11}$ (sugar) and NaCl can be separated by dissolving sugar in alcohol, due to differential solubility.
Statement II : Rose essence from rose petals is seperated by steam distillation due to its high volatility and insolubility in H$_2$O.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
29632.sol:
Statement I : Sugar ($\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}$) is soluble in alcohol, whereas sodium chloride ($\text{NaCl}$) is insoluble in alcohol. Therefore, a mixture of sugar and salt can be separated based on their differential solubility in alcohol. This statement is true.

Statement II : Steam distillation is used to separate and purify organic compounds that are steam volatile and immiscible (insoluble) in water. Rose essence (essential oil) from rose petals possesses these properties, making steam distillation the appropriate method for its extraction. This statement is also true.

Therefore, both Statement I and Statement II are true.

Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

29696.text:
Identify correct statement/s :
(A) $-\mathrm{OCH}_3$ and $-\mathrm{NHCOCH}_3$ are activating group.
(B) -CN and -OH are meta directing group.
(C) -CN and $-\mathrm{SO}_3 \mathrm{H}$ are meta directing group.
(D) Activating groups act as ortho - and para directing groups.
(E) Halides are activating groups.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
29696.sol:
$-\mathrm{OCH}_3, \mathrm{NHCOCH}_3$ and -OH are activating groups because the atom directly bonded to benzene ring activates the ring by +R effect using its lone pair of electrons. Activating groups are ortho- and para directing groups.
-CN and $-\mathrm{SO}_3 \mathrm{H}$ are deactivating groups because the atom directly bonded to benzene is bonded to more electronegative atom through multiple bonds and they are meta directing groups due to -R effect. Halides are deactivating groups due to -I effect.

30732.subject: Chemistry
30732.text: $20$ mL of a solution of acetic acid required $28.4$ mL of $0.1$ M NaOH for its neutralization. A solution (X) was prepared by mixing $20$ mL of the above acetic acid and $14.2$ mL of $0.1$ M NaOH solution. What is the pH of the solution (X)? ($pK_a$ value of acetic acid is $4.75$).
30732.sol:
For complete neutralization of $20$ mL of acetic acid, the millimoles of NaOH required is:

$28.4 \times 0.1 = 2.84$ mmol

Thus, $20$ mL of the acetic acid solution contains $2.84$ mmol of $CH_3COOH$.

For the preparation of solution (X), the millimoles of NaOH added is:

$14.2 \times 0.1 = 1.42$ mmol

The reaction between acetic acid and sodium hydroxide is:

$CH_3COOH + NaOH \rightarrow CH_3COONa + H_2O$

Millimoles of $CH_3COOH$ remaining after the reaction = $2.84 - 1.42 = 1.42$ mmol

Millimoles of $CH_3COONa$ formed = $1.42$ mmol

Since the solution contains a weak acid and its conjugate base, it forms an acidic buffer. Using the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation:

$pH = pK_a + \log \left( \dfrac{[\text{Salt}]}{[\text{Acid}]} \right)$

Substituting the values:

$pH = 4.75 + \log \left( \dfrac{1.42}{1.42} \right)$

$pH = 4.75 + \log(1)$

$pH = 4.75$

Answer: $4.75$

30850.text: Which one of the following arrangements represents the correct order of the proton affinity of the given species :
30850.sol:
The species with the greatest proton affinity will be the strongest base, and its conjugate acid will be the weakest acid. The weakest acid will have the smallest value of $\mathrm{K}_a$. Since $\mathrm{HI}$ is a stronger acid than $\mathrm{HF}$ which is a stronger acid than $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{S}$, a partial order of proton affinity is 
$\mathrm{I}^{-} < \mathrm{F}^{-} < \mathrm{HS}^{-}$
Since $\mathrm{NH}_3$ is a very weak acid, $\mathrm{NH}_2^{-}$must be a very strong base. Therefore the correct order of proton affinity is
$\mathrm{I}^{-} < \mathrm{F}^{-} < \mathrm{HS}^{-} < \mathrm{NH}_2^{-}$

34318.text:
Let $f: \left(0, 2\right) \to R$ be defined as $f\left(x\right) = {\log}_{2}\left(1 + tan\left(\dfrac{\pix}{4}\right)\right)$.

Then, $\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{2}{n}\left(f\left(\dfrac{1}{n}\right) + f\left(\dfrac{2}{n}\right) + \ldots . + f\left(1\right)\right)$ is equal to ________.
34318.sol:
Given $f\left(x\right) = {\log}_{2}\left(1 + tan\left(\dfrac{\pix}{4}\right)\right) = \dfrac{{\log}_{e}\left(1 + tan\left(\dfrac{\pix}{4}\right)\right)}{{\log}_{e}2}$

$E = 2\lim_{n \to \infty}\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}\dfrac{1}{n}f\left(\dfrac{r}{n}\right)$

$E = \dfrac{2}{{\log}_{e}2}{∫}_{0}^{1}{\log}_{e}\left(1 + tan\dfrac{\pix}{4}\right)dx$ $. . . ( i )$

Replacing $x \to 1 - x$

$E = \dfrac{2}{{\log}_{e}2}{∫}_{0}^{1}{\log}_{e}\left(1 + tan\dfrac{\pi}{4}\left(1 - x\right)\right)dx$

$E = \dfrac{2}{{\log}_{e}2}{∫}_{0}^{1}{\log}_{e}\left(1 + tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}x\right)\right)dx$

$E = \dfrac{2}{{\log}_{e}2}{∫}_{0}^{1}{\log}_{e}\left(1 + \dfrac{1 - tan\dfrac{\pi}{4}x}{1 + tan\dfrac{\pi}{4}x}\right)dx$

$E = \dfrac{2}{{\log}_{e}2}{∫}_{0}^{1}{\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{2}{1 + tan\dfrac{\pix}{4}}\right)dx$

$E = \dfrac{2}{{\log}_{e}2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\left({\log}_{e}2 - {\log}_{e}\left(1 + tan\dfrac{\pix}{4}\right)\right)dx$ $. . . ( ii )$

Adding an equation $( i ) \text{ and } ( ii )$ we get,

$E = 1$

34456.text:
If the system of linear equations :
$\begin{aligned}
& x+y+2 z=6 \\
& 2 x+3 y+\mathrm{a} z=\mathrm{a}+1 \\
& -x-3 y+\mathrm{b} z=2 \mathrm{~b}
\end{aligned}$
where $a, b \in \mathbf{R}$, has infinitely many solutions, then $7 a+3 b$ is equal to :
34456.sol:
The given equations are
$\begin{aligned}
& x+y+2 z=6 \\
& 2 x+3 y+a z=a+1 \\
& -x-3 y+b z=2 b, \text{ where } a, b, \in \mathbf{R}
\end{aligned}$

For infinite many solutions:
$D=D_1=D_2=D_3=0 \begin{aligned}
& \therefore D=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 1 & 2 \\
2 & 3 & a \\
-1 & -3 & b
\end{array}\right|=2 a+b-6 \\
& D_1=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
6 & 1 & 2 \\
a+1 & 3 & a \\
2 b & -3 & b
\end{array}\right|=12 a+5 b+a b-6 \\
& D_2=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 6 & 2 \\
2 & a+1 & a \\
-1 & 2 b & b
\end{array}\right|=-4 a-3 b-a b+2 \\
& \text{ and } D_3=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 1 & 6 \\
2 & 3 & a+1 \\
-1 & -3 & 2 b
\end{array}\right|=2 a+2 b-16
\end{aligned}$
from above relations
$\begin{aligned}
& a=-2, b=10 \\
& \therefore 7 a+3 b=16
\end{aligned}$

34739.text: Let $y = {y}_{1}\left(x\right)$ and $y = {y}_{2}\left(x\right)$ be two distinct solutions of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x + y$, with ${y}_{1}\left(0\right) = 0$ and ${y}_{2}\left(0\right) = 1$ respectively. Then, the number of points of intersection of $y = {y}_{1}\left(x\right)$ and $y = {y}_{2}\left(x\right)$ is
34739.sol:
Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x + y ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = x$

So, $IF = {e}^{∫ - 1dx} = {e}^{- x}$

Now solution is given by $y{e}^{- x} = ∫ x{e}^{- x}dx$

$⇒ y{e}^{- x} = - x{e}^{- x} - {e}^{- x} + c$

$⇒ y = - x - 1 + c{e}^{x}$

Given, ${y}_{1}\left(0\right) = 0 ⇒ c = 1$

$∴ {y}_{1} = - x - 1 + {e}^{x} ⋯ \left(1\right)$

Also given ${y}_{2}\left(0\right) = 1 ⇒ c = 2$

$∴ {y}_{2} = - x - 1 + 2{e}^{x} ⋯ \left(2\right)$

Now from equation $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right) we get, ${y}_{2} - {y}_{1} = {e}^{x} > 0 ∴ {y}_{2} \ne {y}_{1}$

$∴$ Number of points of intersection of ${y}_{1} and {y}_{2}$ is zero.

$

36181.subject: Mathematics
36181.text: Let the parabola $y = x^2 + px + q$ passing through the point $(1, -1)$ be such that the distance between its vertex and the $x$-axis is minimum. Then the value of $p^2 + q^2$ is:
36181.sol:
Given the equation of the parabola $y = x^2 + px + q$.

Since it passes through $(1, -1)$, we have:

$-1 = 1 + p + q \Rightarrow q = -p - 2$

The vertex of the parabola $y = x^2 + px + q$ occurs at $x = -\dfrac{p}{2}$.

The $y$-coordinate of the vertex is:

$y_v = \left(-\dfrac{p}{2}\right)^2 + p\left(-\dfrac{p}{2}\right) + q = -\dfrac{p^2}{4} + q$

The distance between the vertex and the $x$-axis is $|y_v|$. Substituting $q = -p - 2$ into the expression for $y_v$:

$|y_v| = \left|-\dfrac{p^2}{4} - p - 2\right| = \dfrac{1}{4}|p^2 + 4p + 8| = \dfrac{1}{4}|(p+2)^2 + 4|$

To minimize this distance, the term $(p+2)^2$ must be minimum. Since $(p+2)^2 \ge 0$ for all real $p$, the minimum value occurs at $p = -2$.

Substituting $p = -2$ into $q = -p - 2$, we get:

$q = -(-2) - 2 = 0$

Therefore, the value of $p^2 + q^2$ is:

$p^2 + q^2 = (-2)^2 + 0^2 = 4$

Answer: $4$

37016.text: For the functions $f(\theta) = \alpha\tan^2\theta + \beta\cot^2\theta$, and $g(\theta) = \alpha\sin^2\theta + \beta\cos^2\theta$, $\alpha > \beta > 0$, let $\min_{0 < \theta < \pi/2}f(\theta) = \max_{0 < \theta < \pi}g(\theta)$. If the first term of a G.P. is $\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2\beta}\right)$, its common ratio is $\left(\dfrac{2\beta}{\alpha}\right)$ and the sum of its first $10$ terms is $\dfrac{m}{n}$, $\gcd(m, n) = 1$, then $m + n$ is equal to _______.
37016.sol:
For the function $f(\theta) = \alpha\tan^2\theta + \beta\cot^2\theta$, applying the AM-GM inequality gives:

$\alpha\tan^2\theta + \beta\cot^2\theta \ge 2\sqrt{\alpha\tan^2\theta \cdot \beta\cot^2\theta} = 2\sqrt{\alpha\beta}$

Thus, $\min_{0 < \theta < \pi/2} f(\theta) = 2\sqrt{\alpha\beta}$.

For the function $g(\theta) = \alpha\sin^2\theta + \beta\cos^2\theta$, we can rewrite it as:

$g(\theta) = \alpha\sin^2\theta + \beta(1 - \sin^2\theta) = \beta + (\alpha - \beta)\sin^2\theta$

Since $\alpha > \beta > 0$, the maximum value of $g(\theta)$ occurs when $\sin^2\theta$ is maximum, which is $1$ (at $\theta = \pi/2$).

Thus, $\max_{0 < \theta < \pi} g(\theta) = \beta + (\alpha - \beta)(1) = \alpha$.

Given that $\min f(\theta) = \max g(\theta)$, we have:

$2\sqrt{\alpha\beta} = \alpha$

Squaring both sides (since $\alpha > 0$), we get:

$4\alpha\beta = \alpha^2 \Rightarrow \alpha = 4\beta$

For the given Geometric Progression (G.P.):

First term $a = \dfrac{\alpha}{2\beta} = \dfrac{4\beta}{2\beta} = 2$

Common ratio $r = \dfrac{2\beta}{\alpha} = \dfrac{2\beta}{4\beta} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

The sum of the first $10$ terms is:

$S_{10} = a\dfrac{1 - r^{10}}{1 - r} = 2\dfrac{1 - (1/2)^{10}}{1 - 1/2} = 4\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{1024}\right) = 4\left(\dfrac{1023}{1024}\right) = \dfrac{1023}{256}$

We are given $S_{10} = \dfrac{m}{n}$ with $\gcd(m, n) = 1$.

Since $256 = 2^8$ and $1023$ is odd, they are coprime. Therefore, $m = 1023$ and $n = 256$.

$m + n = 1023 + 256 = 1279$

Answer: $1279$

40809.subject: Physics
40809.text: The height in terms of radius of the earth $(R)$, at which the acceleration due to gravity becomes $\dfrac{g}{9}$, where $g$ is acceleration due to gravity on earth's surface, is ______.
40809.sol:
The acceleration due to gravity at a height $h$ above the surface of the earth is given by

$g' = \dfrac{g}{\left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right)^2}$

Given that $g' = \dfrac{g}{9}$, we get

$\dfrac{g}{9} = \dfrac{g}{\left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right)^2}$

$\left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right)^2 = 9$

$1 + \dfrac{h}{R} = 3$

$\dfrac{h}{R} = 2$

$h = 2R$

Answer: $2R$

40860.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I : Rotation of the earth shows effect on the value of acceleration due to gravity $( g )$.

Statement II : The effect of rotation of the earth on the value of $g$ at the equator is minimum and that at the pole is maximum.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is false but statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but statement II is false
40860.sol:
The variation of acceleration due to gravity with the rotation of Earth can be written as

$g ' = g - {\omega}^{2}R\cos^{2}\lambda . . . \left(1\right)$

Substitute $0 °$ for $\lambda$ for equatorial position to obtain the acceleration due to gravity.

$\begin{cases}g ' & = & g - {\omega}^{2}R\cos^{2}0 ° \\ & = & g - {\omega}^{2}R\end{cases}$

Substitute $90 °$ for $\lambda$ for polar position to obtain the acceleration due to gravity.

$\begin{cases}g ' & = & g - {\omega}^{2}R\cos^{2}90 ° \\ & = & g\end{cases}$

The above two equations show that the effect on acceleration due to gravity is maximum at the equator and minimum at pole.

Let $R$ be the radius of bigger drop and $r$ be the radius of smaller drop.

$⇒ R = 10r$

As surface energy is stated as $u = SA$, here, $S$ is surface tension and $A$ is surface area.

Thus, ${u}_{i} = S\left(4\pi{R}^{2}\right)$ and ${u}_{f} = S\left(4\pi{r}^{2}\right) \times 1000$

The ratio is $\dfrac{{u}_{f}}{{u}_{i}} = \dfrac{1000{r}^{2}}{{R}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{u}_{f}}{{u}_{i}} = \dfrac{10}{1}$

Hence, the value of $x = 1$.

44207.subject: Physics
44207.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : In a Young's double slit experiment, the angular separation of fringes will increase as the screen is moved away from the plane of the slits
Statement II: In a Young's double slit experiment, the angular separation of fringes will increase when monochromatic source is replaced by another monochromatic source of higher wavelength.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
44207.sol:
In Young's double slit experiment, angular separation of fringes is $\beta = \frac{\lambda}{d}$ where $\lambda$ is wavelength and d is slit separation.
Statement I is false because angular separation is independent of screen distance; it depends only on the slit separation and wavelength.
Statement II is true because increasing the wavelength directly increases the angular separation $\beta$.
Therefore, Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

46353.subject: Physics
46353.text: The turns of a solenoid, designed to provide a given magnetic flux density along its axis, are wound to fill the space between two concentric cylinders of fixed radii. How should the diameter $d$ of the wire used be chosen so as to minimize the heat dissipated in the windings?
options: Wire should be multiple of $5 d$
46353.sol: The cross-sectional area of the space to be filled is fixed, whilst that of the wire varies as $d^2$. Thus, $n \propto d^{-2}$. The resistance of one turn is inversely proportional to the cross-sectional area of the wire, i.e. varies as $d^{-2}$ and hence the resistance per unit length of the solenoid is $R \propto n d^{-2} \propto d^{-4}$. The flux density $B$ is $\propto n I$ and therefore the required current $I \propto n^{-1} \propto d^2$. The heat dissipated per unit length is $R I^2$, which $\propto d^{-4}\left(d^2\right)^2$, i.e. independent of $d$. Thus, within limits, it does not matter what diameter wire is chosen so far as the heating effect is concerned.

46416.subject: Physics
46416.text: A ball is thrown upwards with a speed $u$ from a height h above the ground. The time taken by the ball to hit the ground is
46416.sol:
Time taken to reach the highest point from the height h is obtained from equation, $\mathrm{v}=\mathrm{u}-\mathrm{gt}$
$\therefore \quad 0=\mathrm{u}-\mathrm{gt}$ or $\mathrm{t}=\frac{\mathrm{u}}{\mathrm{g}}$
Height attained above h is obtained from
$\mathrm{v}^2-\mathrm{u}^2=2(-\mathrm{g}) \mathrm{h}_1$
or $\quad 0-\mathrm{u}^2=2(-\mathrm{g}) \mathrm{h}_1$ or $\mathrm{h}_1=\frac{\mathrm{u}^2}{2 \mathrm{~g}}$
Total height, $\mathrm{h}_2=\left[\mathrm{h}_1+\mathrm{h}=\frac{\mathrm{u}^2}{2 \mathrm{~g}}+\mathrm{h}\right]$
Time taken to hit the ground is obtained from,
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{h}_2 & =\mathrm{ut}+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{at}^2 \\ \frac{\mathrm{u}^2}{2 \mathrm{~g}}+\mathrm{h} & =0+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{gt}^2\end{aligned}$
$\therefore$ Total time taken, $\mathrm{t}=\sqrt{\frac{\left(\mathrm{u}^2+2 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~h}\right)}{\mathrm{g}^2}}$

55790.subject: Chemistry
55790.text: Identify the correct statement regarding geometry and lone pair of electrons present in $\mathrm{CH}_4$ and $\mathrm{SiCl}_4$
options: Both have same geometry with two lone pair of electrons each.
Both have different geometry with one lone pair of electrons each.
Both have same geometry with no lone pair of electrons each.
Both have different geometry with no lone pair of electrons each.
55790.sol:
Using VSEPR theory to analyze molecular geometry:

For $\mathrm{CH_4}$ and $\mathrm{SiCl_4}$, both central atoms ($\mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{Si}$) belong to Group 14 and have 4 valence electrons, forming 4 single bonds with no remaining electrons for lone pairs. The steric number is 4 in both cases, resulting in tetrahedral geometry.

Comparing the options:

A) Incorrect: both have zero lone pairs
B) Incorrect: geometries are identical, not different
C) Correct: both exhibit tetrahedral geometry with no lone pairs
D) Incorrect: geometries are identical, not different

The correct answer is $\boxed{C}$.

56855.subject: Chemistry
56855.text: If standard reduction potential $\left(\mathrm{E}^{\circ}\right)$ of $\left(\mathrm{Mg}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+2} \mid \mathrm{Mg}_{(\mathrm{s})}\right)$, $\left(\mathrm{Ag}^{+}{ }_{(\mathrm{aq})} \mid \mathrm{Ag}_{(\mathrm{s})}\right),\left(\mathrm{Zn}^{+2}{ }_{(\mathrm{aq})} \mid \mathrm{Zn}_{(\mathrm{s})}\right)$ and $\left(\mathrm{Cu}^{+2}{ }_{(\mathrm{aq})} \mid \mathrm{Cu}_{(\mathrm{s})}\right)$ are -2.37 V , $+0.79 \mathrm{~V},-0.76 \mathrm{~V}$ and +0.34 V respectively. Which of the following reaction is spontaneous?
56855.sol:
A reaction is spontaneous if its standard cell potential $E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} > 0$, where $E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = E^{\circ}_{\text{reduction}}(\text{cathode}) - E^{\circ}_{\text{reduction}}(\text{anode})$.

Using the standard reduction potentials: $E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Mg}^{+2} \mid \mathrm{Mg}) = -2.37\ \mathrm{V}$, $E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Ag}^{+} \mid \mathrm{Ag}) = +0.79\ \mathrm{V}$, $E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Zn}^{+2} \mid \mathrm{Zn}) = -0.76\ \mathrm{V}$, and $E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Cu}^{+2} \mid \mathrm{Cu}) = +0.34\ \mathrm{V}$:

For reaction A: $\mathrm{Zn}_{(\mathrm{s})}+\mathrm{Mg}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+2} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Zn}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+2}+\mathrm{Mg}_{(\mathrm{s})}$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Mg}^{+2}) - E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Zn}^{+2}) = -2.37 - (-0.76) = -1.61\ \mathrm{V}$
Spontaneous? No

For reaction B: $2\mathrm{Ag}_{(\mathrm{s})}+\mathrm{Zn}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+2} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Ag}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+}+\mathrm{Zn}_{(\mathrm{s})}$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Zn}^{+2}) - E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Ag}^{+}) = -0.76 - 0.79 = -1.55\ \mathrm{V}$
Spontaneous? No

For reaction C: $\mathrm{Zn}_{(\mathrm{s})}+\mathrm{Cu}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+2} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Zn}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+2}+\mathrm{Cu}_{(\mathrm{s})}$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Cu}^{+2}) - E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Zn}^{+2}) = 0.34 - (-0.76) = 1.10\ \mathrm{V}$
Spontaneous? Yes

For reaction D: $\mathrm{Cu}_{(\mathrm{s})}+\mathrm{Mg}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+2} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+2}+\mathrm{Mg}_{(\mathrm{s})}$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Mg}^{+2}) - E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Cu}^{+2}) = -2.37 - 0.34 = -2.71\ \mathrm{V}$
Spontaneous? No

The only spontaneous reaction is C.

57130.subject: Chemistry
57130.text: What is IUPAC name of following compound?
57130.sol:
The principal functional group in the given compound is the carboxylic acid group ($-COOH$). Therefore, the parent chain is taken as benzoic acid.

Numbering of the benzene ring starts from the carbon atom attached to the $-COOH$ group as position 1. To give the lowest possible number to the substituent, the carbon attached to the methyl group ($-CH_3$) is numbered as 2.

Thus, there is a methyl group at the 2-position of the benzoic acid ring. The IUPAC name of the compound is 2-Methylbenzoic acid. (Note: o-Toluic acid is its common name).

Answer: 2-Methylbenzoic acid

58248.subject: Chemistry
58248.text: Identify false statement from the following about fluorine.
options: It has high bond dissociation enthalpy among all halogens.
58248.sol:
Analysis of statements about fluorine:

Fluorine is the most electronegative element (Pauling scale 3.98), confirming statement A is true.

Due to its extreme electronegativity, fluorine cannot exhibit positive oxidation states and maintains only a -1 oxidation state, making statement B true.

The order of bond dissociation enthalpy is $\text{Cl}_2$ (242 kJ/mol) $ > \text{Br}_2$ (193 kJ/mol) $ > \text{F}_2$ (158 kJ/mol) $ > \text{I}_2$ (151 kJ/mol). Interelectronic repulsions between lone pairs in $\text{F}_2$ weaken its bond, making it lower than chlorine and bromine. Statement C is false.

Fluorine forms only hypofluorous acid (HOF) as its oxoacid, lacking d-orbitals for octet expansion, confirming statement D is true.

59892.subject: Chemistry
59892.text: Which of the following properties of a system depends upon the amount of matter and path?
59892.sol:
Properties that depend on the amount of matter present in the system are known as extensive properties.

Properties whose values depend on the specific path taken to go from the initial state to the final state are known as path functions.

Free energy, enthalpy, and entropy are state functions, meaning their values depend only on the initial and final states of the system and are independent of the path followed.

Heat is a path function because the amount of heat exchanged depends on the process or path taken. It also depends on the amount of matter (extensive in nature), as the heat required to change the state of a system is proportional to its mass or number of moles (q = mc\Delta T$).

Answer: Heat$

Let $f(x) = x^{\dfrac{1}{3}}$

Let $x = 0.008$ and $\Delta x = -0.001$

$f(x) = (0.008)^{\dfrac{1}{3}} = 0.2 = \dfrac{1}{5}$

$f(0.007) \approx \dfrac{1}{5} + \left(\dfrac{25}{3}\right)(-0.001)$

$f(0.007) \approx \dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{25}{3000}$

$f(0.007) \approx \dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{1}{120}$

$f(0.007) \approx \dfrac{24 - 1}{120} = \dfrac{23}{120}$

60717.subject: Mathematics
60717.text: The angle between the tangents drawn from the origin to the circle $(x-7)^2 + (y+1)^2 = 25$ is
60717.sol:
The equation of the circle is $(x-7)^2 + (y+1)^2 = 25$.

The center of the circle is $C(7,-1)$ and its radius is $r = 5$.

Let the tangents be drawn from the origin $O(0,0)$ and the angle between them be $2\theta$.

The distance between the origin and the center of the circle is $OC = \sqrt{(7-0)^2 + (-1-0)^2} = \sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt{2}$.

From the right-angled triangle formed by the origin, the center, and the point of contact, we have $\sin \theta = \dfrac{r}{OC}$.

$\sin \theta = \dfrac{5}{5\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\theta = 45^{}^{\circ}$

The angle between the tangents is $2\theta = 90^{}^{\circ}$.

64376.text: The vector equation of plane in parametric form, passing through the points (-1, 2, 0), (2, 2, -1) and parallel to the line $\dfrac{x-1}{1} = \dfrac{2y+1}{2} = \dfrac{z+1}{-1} is$
64376.sol:
The position vector of the point $A(-1, 2, 0)$ is $\vec{a} = -\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}$.

The plane passes through $A(-1, 2, 0)$ and $B(2, 2, -1)$. A vector parallel to the plane is $\vec{AB} = (2 - (-1))\hat{i} + (2 - 2)\hat{j} + (-1 - 0)\hat{k} = 3\hat{i} - \hat{k}$.

The given line is $\dfrac{x-1}{1} = \dfrac{2y+1}{2} = \dfrac{z+1}{-1}$. Rewriting it in standard form, we get $\dfrac{x-1}{1} = \dfrac{y+1/2}{1} = \dfrac{z+1}{-1}$.

The direction vector of the line is $\vec{v} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$. Since the plane is parallel to this line, $\vec{v}$ is also parallel to the plane.

The parametric vector equation of a plane passing through a point with position vector $\vec{a}$ and parallel to two non-collinear vectors $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ is given by $\vec{r} = \vec{a} + \lambda\vec{b} + \mu\vec{c}$.

Substituting $\vec{a} = -\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}$, $\vec{b} = \vec{AB} = 3\hat{i} - \hat{k}$, and $\vec{c} = \vec{v} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$, we get:

$\vec{r} = (-\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}) + \lambda(3\hat{i} - \hat{k}) + \mu(\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k})$

Answer: $\bar{r} = (-\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}) + \lambda(3\hat{i} - \hat{k}) + \mu(\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k})$

64402.text: If the lines $\dfrac{x-1}{2} = \dfrac{y+1}{3} = \dfrac{z-1}{4}$ and $\dfrac{x-3}{1} = \dfrac{y-c}{2} = \dfrac{z}{1}$ intersect, then the radius of circle $x^2 + y^2 - 4x + 10y + c = 0$ is
64402.sol:
The condition for the two lines to intersect is that they must be coplanar.

$\begin{vmatrix} 3-1 \text{ and } c-(-1) \text{ and } 0-1 \\ 2 \text{ and } 3 \text{ and } 4 \\ 1 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } 1 \end{vmatrix} = 0$

$\begin{vmatrix} 2 \text{ and } c+1 \text{ and } -1 \\ 2 \text{ and } 3 \text{ and } 4 \\ 1 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } 1 \end{vmatrix} = 0$

Expanding the determinant along the first row:

$2(3 - 8) - (c+1)(2 - 4) - 1(4 - 3) = 0$

$-10 + 2(c+1) - 1 = 0$

$2c - 9 = 0 \Rightarrow c = \dfrac{9}{2}$

The equation of the circle is $x^2 + y^2 - 4x + 10y + \dfrac{9}{2} = 0$.

The radius of the circle is given by $r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}$.

$r = \sqrt{(-2)^2 + (5)^2 - \dfrac{9}{2}}$

$r = \sqrt{4 + 25 - \dfrac{9}{2}}$

$r = \sqrt{29 - \dfrac{9}{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{49}{2}} = \dfrac{7}{\sqrt{2}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{7}{\sqrt{2}}$

65149.text: If $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ are three coplanar vectors such that $|\bar{a}|=1,|\bar{b}|=2$, $\overline{\mathrm{b}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}=8$, the angle between $\overline{\mathrm{b}}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ is $45^{{}^{\circ}}$, then $|\bar{a} \times(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})|=$
65149.sol:
Given vectors $\bar{a}$, $\bar{b}$, $\bar{c}$ are coplanar with $|\bar{a}| = 1$, $|\bar{b}| = 2$, $\bar{b} \cdot \bar{c} = 8$, and the angle between $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$ is $45^{{}^{\circ}}$.

To determine $\bar{c}$'s magnitude, apply the dot product definition: $\bar{b} \cdot \bar{c} = |\bar{b}| |\bar{c}| \cos \theta$.
Substitute known values: $8 = 2 |\bar{c}| \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, leading to $|\bar{c}| = 4\sqrt{2}$.

Since the vectors are coplanar, $\bar{a}$ lies in the plane formed by $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$, while $\bar{b} \times \bar{c}$ is perpendicular to this plane.
Thus, the angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b} \times \bar{c}$ is $90^{{}^{\circ}}$.

The magnitude of the cross product is evaluated as:
$|\bar{a} \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c})| = |\bar{a}| \cdot |\bar{b} \times \bar{c}| \cdot \sin 90^{{}^{\circ}} = |\bar{b} \times \bar{c}|$.

Compute $|\bar{b} \times \bar{c}| = |\bar{b}| \cdot |\bar{c}| \cdot \sin 45^{{}^{\circ}} = 2 \cdot 4\sqrt{2} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 8$.

Therefore, $|\bar{a} \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c})| = 8$.

65191.text: If the projection of $\bar{a}$ on $\bar{b}+\bar{c}$ is twice the projection of $\bar{b}+\bar{c}$ on $\bar{a}$ also if $|\bar{b}|=2 \sqrt{2},|\bar{c}|=4$ and the angle between $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$ is $\frac{\pi}{4}$ then $|\bar{a}|=$
65191.sol:
The projection of $\bar{a}$ on $(\bar{b}+\bar{c})$ is twice that of $(\bar{b}+\bar{c})$ on $\bar{a}$, yielding the relation:

$\frac{\bar{a} \cdot (\bar{b}+\bar{c})}{|\bar{b}+\bar{c}|} = 2 \cdot \frac{\bar{a} \cdot (\bar{b}+\bar{c})}{|\bar{a}|}$

Canceling the common nonzero dot product and simplifying gives:

$|\bar{a}| = 2 |\bar{b}+\bar{c}|$

The magnitude of $\bar{b}+\bar{c}$ is computed using the given data: $|\bar{b}| = 2\sqrt{2}$, $|\bar{c}| = 4$, and $\theta = \frac{\pi}{4}$.

$|\bar{b}+\bar{c}|^2 = |\bar{b}|^2 + |\bar{c}|^2 + 2 \bar{b} \cdot \bar{c} = (2\sqrt{2})^2 + 4^2 + 2 \cdot (2\sqrt{2} \cdot 4 \cdot \cos\frac{\pi}{4})$

$|\bar{b}+\bar{c}|^2 = 8 + 16 + 2 (8\sqrt{2} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}) = 24 + 16 = 40$

Thus $|\bar{b}+\bar{c}| = \sqrt{40} = 2\sqrt{10}$, and substituting into the earlier relation gives:

$|\bar{a}| = 2 \cdot 2\sqrt{10} = 4\sqrt{10}$

Answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

66557.subject: Physics
66557.text: Photoelectric emission is observed from a metallic surface for frequencies $v_1$ and $v_2$ of the incident light rays (v_1 > v_2$). If the maximum values of kinetic energy of the photoelectrons emitted in the two cases are in the ratio of $k : 1$, then what is the threshold frequency of the metallic surface?$
66557.sol:
Using Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons is given by $K = h(v - v_0)$, where $v_0$ is the threshold frequency.

For frequency $v_1$, $K_1 = h(v_1 - v_0)$

For frequency $v_2$, $K_2 = h(v_2 - v_0)$

Given that the ratio of maximum kinetic energies is $k : 1$, we have:

$\dfrac{K_1}{K_2} = \dfrac{h(v_1 - v_0)}{h(v_2 - v_0)} = k$

$\dfrac{v_1 - v_0}{v_2 - v_0} = k$

$v_1 - v_0 = k(v_2 - v_0)$

$v_1 - v_0 = kv_2 - kv_0$

$kv_0 - v_0 = kv_2 - v_1$

$v_0(k - 1) = kv_2 - v_1$

$v_0 = \dfrac{kv_2 - v_1}{k - 1}$

Answer: $\dfrac{kv_2 - v_1}{k - 1}$

67208.subject: Physics
67208.text: The lengths of seconds pendulums on the surface of the earth and at an altitude '$h$' from the surface of the earth are $l_s$ and $l_h$ respectively. The radius of the earth is
67208.sol:
The time period of a simple pendulum is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}$.

For a seconds pendulum, the time period is constant ($T = 2$ s) at both locations.

Therefore, $T_s = T_h \Rightarrow 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{l_s}{g_s}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{l_h}{g_h}}$.

This gives $\dfrac{l_s}{l_h} = \dfrac{g_s}{g_h}$.

The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the earth is $g_s = \dfrac{GM}{R^2}$ and at an altitude $h$ is $g_h = \dfrac{GM}{(R+h)^2}$.

Substituting these values, we get:

$\dfrac{l_s}{l_h} = \dfrac{\dfrac{GM}{R^2}}{\dfrac{GM}{(R+h)^2}} = \dfrac{(R+h)^2}{R^2} = \left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right)^2$

Taking the square root on both sides:

$\sqrt{\dfrac{l_s}{l_h}} = 1 + \dfrac{h}{R}$

$\dfrac{h}{R} = \dfrac{\sqrt{l_s}}{\sqrt{l_h}} - 1 = \dfrac{\sqrt{l_s} - \sqrt{l_h}}{\sqrt{l_h}}$

$R = \dfrac{h\sqrt{l_h}}{\sqrt{l_s} - \sqrt{l_h}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{h\sqrt{l_h}}{\sqrt{l_s}-\sqrt{l_h}}$

67360.subject: Physics
67360.text: What is the minimum energy required to launch a satellite of mass ‘m’ from the surface of the earth of mass ‘M’ and radius ‘R’ at an attitude 2R?
67360.sol:
The minimum energy required to launch a satellite from surface of earth is equal to the amount of work done against gravity to move it from the surface of earth to a height h and is given by
$U = W = GMm\left(\dfrac{1}{{r}_{1}} - \dfrac{1}{{r}_{2}}\right)$
$= GMm\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{R + h}\right)$
Here, h = 2R
$⇒ U = GMm\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{3R}\right) = \dfrac{2GMm}{3R}$

68942.text: Refractive index of a glass convex lens is $1.5$. The radius of curvature of each of the two surfaces of the lens is 40 cm. The ratio of the power of the lens when immersed in a liquid of refractive index $1.25$ to that when placed in air is
68942.sol:
The power of a lens is given by the lens maker's formula:

$P = \dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu_{rel} - 1) \left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)

When the $lens is placed in air, the relative refractive index is\mu_{rel} =$\dfrac{\mu_g}{\mu_a} = \dfrac{1.5}{1} =1.5$.

The power in air is:

$P_a = (1.5 - 1) \left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right) =$0.5$\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)

When the $lens is immersed in the liquid, the relative refractive index is\mu_{rel} =$\dfrac{\mu_g}{\mu_l} = \dfrac{1.5}{1.25} =$1.2$.

The power in the liquid is:

$P_l = (1.2 - 1) $\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right) =$0.2$\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$

Taking the ratio of the power of the lens in the liquid to that in air, we get:

$\dfrac{P_l}{P_a} = \dfrac{0.2}{0.5} = \dfrac{2}{5}$

Thus, the required ratio is 2:5$.

Answer: $2:5

69968.text: A tyre of a vehicle is filled with air having pressure 270 kPa at $27^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$. The air pressure in the tyre when the temperature increases to $37^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ is
69968.sol:
Gay-Lussac’s Law applies for a fixed mass of gas at constant volume, with pressure proportional to absolute temperature: $\frac{P_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2}{T_2}$.

Convert temperatures to Kelvin:
$T_1 = 27 + 273 = 300$ K
$T_2 = 37 + 273 = 310$ K

Given $P_1 = 270$ kPa, solve for $P_2$:
$P_2 = P_1 \cdot \frac{T_2}{T_1} = 270 \cdot \frac{310}{300} = 270 \cdot \frac{31}{30} = 279$ kPa

The final pressure is $279$ kPa.

72149.subject: Physics
72149.text: The de Broglie wavelength of an electron with kinetic energy $K_1$ is $\lambda_1$. If the kinetic energy increases to $5K_1$, the new wavelength is $\lambda_2 = x\lambda_1$. The value of $x$ is
72149.sol:
The de Broglie wavelength of an electron is given by $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$

For the initial state, $\lambda_1 = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK_1}}$

For the final state, the kinetic energy is $K_2 = 5K_1$. The new wavelength is:

$\lambda_2 = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m(5K_1)}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK_1}}$

$\lambda_2 = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \lambda_1$

Comparing this with $\lambda_2 = x\lambda_1$, we get $x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}}$

72212.subject: Physics
72212.text: Two point charges $8q$ and $2q$ are located at $x=0$ and $x=L$ respectively. The location of a point on the X-axis from origin, at which the net electric field is zero, is $x$. Value of $x$ is equal to
72212.sol:
Let the point where the net electric field is zero be at a distance $x$ from the origin.

Since both charges are positive, the null point must lie between them. The distance of this point from the charge $8q$ is $x$ and from the charge $2q$ is $L - x$.

Equating the magnitudes of the electric fields produced by both charges at this point:

$\dfrac{k(8q)}{x^2} = \dfrac{k(2q)}{(L - x)^2}$

$\dfrac{4}{x^2} = \dfrac{1}{(L - x)^2}$

Taking the square root on both sides:

$\dfrac{2}{x} = \dfrac{1}{L - x}$

$2(L - x) = x$

$2L - 2x = x$

$3x = 2L$

$x = \dfrac{2L}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2L}{3}$

75162.subject: General Ability
75162.text:
Which of the following statements with reference to L-Wave or Long Wave generated by an earthquake is/are correct?
1. They follow the Earth's circumference
2. They travel at more or less at a constant rate

Select the answer using the code given below:
75162.sol:
L-waves or Long waves are surface waves generated by an earthquake.

They travel along the surface of the Earth, which means they follow the Earth's circumference. Thus, statement 1 is correct.

Unlike body waves (P and S waves) whose velocities increase with depth due to the increasing density and rigidity of the Earth's interior, L-waves travel through the relatively uniform surface layers (crust). Therefore, they travel at a more or less constant rate. Thus, statement 2 is also correct.

Both statements 1 and 2 are correct.

Answer: Both 1 and 2

78578.text:
Consider the following for the four (04) items that follow:
The frequency distribution of height of students of a class is given below:
Height (in cm)Number of Students
160–16212
162–16415
164–16624
166–16813

What is the total number of students whose height is less than or equal to 165 cm?
78578.sol:
The cumulative frequencies for the given class intervals are calculated as follows:

Height $\le 162$ cm: $12$
Height $\le 164$ cm: $12 + 15 = 27$
Height $\le 166$ cm: $27 + 24 = 51$

To find the number of students with height less than or equal to $165$ cm, we use linear interpolation within the class interval $164$–$166$.

The number of students in the interval $164$–$166$ is $24$. Assuming a uniform distribution of frequencies within the class interval, the number of students with height between $164$ cm and $165$ cm is:

$\dfrac{165 - 164}{166 - 164} \times 24 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 24 = 12$

The total number of students whose height is less than or equal to $165$ cm is the sum of students with height $\le 164$ cm and those between $164$ cm and $165$ cm:

$27 + 12 = 39$

Answer: $39$

79248.text: What is $3 \alpha+2 \beta$ equal to if $(2 \hat{i}+6 \hat{j}+27 \hat{k}) \times(\hat{i}+\alpha \hat{j}+\beta \hat{k})$ is a null vector?
79248.sol:
Given that, $(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+6 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+27 \hat{\mathrm{k}}) \times(\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\alpha \hat{\mathrm{j}}+\beta \hat{\mathrm{k}})=0\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\
2 & 6 & 27 \\
1 & \alpha & \beta
\end{array}\right|=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \hat{i}(6 \beta-27 \alpha)-\hat{j}(2 \beta-27)+\hat{k}(2 \alpha-6)=0
\end{aligned}$
Comparing both sides of above equation, we get:-
$\begin{aligned}
& 6 \beta-27 \alpha=0 \Rightarrow 2 \beta=9 \alpha \\
& 2 \beta-27=0 \Rightarrow \beta=\frac{27}{2} \text{ and } 2 \alpha-6=0 \Rightarrow \alpha=3
\end{aligned}$
So, $3 \alpha+2 \beta=3 \times 3+2 \times \frac{27}{2}=9+27=36$

81237.subject: Chemistry
81237.text:
Which of the following complexes exhibits the highest paramagnetic behaviour?
where gly = glycine, en = ethylenediamine and bpy = bipyridyl moities
(At no: $\mathrm{Ti}=22, \mathrm{~V}=23, \mathrm{Fe}=26, \mathrm{Co}=27$ )
81237.sol:
Key Idea : Greater is the number of unpaired electrons, larger is the paramagnetism.
$\begin{aligned}
& {\left[\mathrm{V}(\mathrm{gly})_2(\mathrm{OH})_2\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_2\right]^{+}} \\
& \mathrm{V}_{23}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 4 s^2, 3 d^3
\end{aligned}$
Oxidation state of $\mathrm{V}$ in $\left[\mathrm{V}(\mathrm{gly})_2(\mathrm{OH})_2\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_2\right]^{+}$ is
$\begin{gathered}
x+(-1) \times 2+(-1) \times 2+(0) \times 2=+1 \\
x=+5 \\
\mathrm{~V}^{5+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^0
\end{gathered}$
(No unpaired electron in option (A))
So, option (B),
$\begin{aligned}
& {\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\text{ en) }(\text{ bpy })\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_2\right]^{2+}\right.} \\
& \mathrm{Fe}_{26}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 4 s^2, 3 d^6
\end{aligned}$
Oxidation state of $\mathrm{Fe}$ in $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{en}) \text{ (bpy) }\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_2\right]^{2+}$ is
$\begin{gathered}
x+(0)+(0)+(0) \times 2=+2 \\
x=+2 \\
\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^6
\end{gathered}$
But en, bpy and $\mathrm{NH}_3$ all are strong field ligands so pairing occurs, thus no unpaired electrons.
So, option (C),
$\begin{gathered}
{\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{OX})_2(\mathrm{OH}]_2\right]^{-}} \\
\mathrm{Co}_{27}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 4 s^2, 3 d^7
\end{gathered}$
Oxidation state of $\mathrm{Co}$ in $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{OX})_2(\mathrm{OH})_2\right]^{-}$is
$x+(-2) \times 2+(-1) \times 2=-1$
$\begin{aligned}
& x-6=-1 \\
& x=+5 \\
& \mathrm{Co}^{5+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^4 \\
& \text{(4 paired electrons)} \\
& \text{Now, option (D),} \\
& {\left[\mathrm{Ti}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}} \\
& \mathrm{Ti}_{22}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 4 s^2, 3 d^2
\end{aligned}$
$\mathrm{Ti}_{22}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 4 s^2, 3 d^2$
Oxidation state of Ti in $\left[\mathrm{Ti}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ is +3, thus it contains 1 unpaired electron.
Hence, $\quad\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{OX})_2(\mathrm{OH})_2\right]^{-}$has highest paramagnetic behaviour.

83417.subject: Physics
83417.text: Two discs of same moment of inertia $( I ) $ are rotating in same sense about their regular axis passing through centre and perpendicular to the plane of disc with angular velocities ${\omega}_{1}$ and ${\omega}_{2}$. They are brought into contact face to face coinciding the axis of rotation. The expression for loss in energy during this process is
83417.sol:
The initial angular momentum of two discs is ${I}_{1}{\omega}_{1} + {I}_{2}{\omega}_{2} = I\left({\omega}_{1} + {\omega}_{2}\right)$.

The final angular momentum of system is $\left({I}_{1} + {I}_{2}\right)\omega = 2I\omega$

From the conservation of angular momentum, $\omega = \dfrac{{\omega}_{1} + {\omega}_{2}}{2}$.

Initial kinetic energy, $K{E}_{i} = \dfrac{1}{2}I\left({\omega}_{1}^{2} + {\omega}_{2}^{2}\right)$

and final kinetic energy, $K{E}_{f} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(2I\right)\dfrac{{\left({\omega}_{1} + {\omega}_{2}\right)}^{2}}{4}$

Loss in kinetic energy is $\DeltaKE = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{{I}_{1}{I}_{2}}{{I}_{1} + {I}_{2}}{\left({\omega}_{1} - {\omega}_{2}\right)}^{2}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{{I}^{2}}{\left(2I\right)}{\left({\omega}_{1} - {\omega}_{2}\right)}^{2}$

$= \dfrac{1}{4}I{\left({\omega}_{1} - {\omega}_{2}\right)}^{2}$

83779.text: The two nearest harmonics of a tube closed at one end and open at other end are 220 Hz and 260 Hz. What is the fundamental frequency of the system?
83779.sol:
Two successive frequencies of closed pipe

$\dfrac{nv}{4l} = 220$ ....(i)

$\dfrac{\left(n + 2\right)v}{4l} = 260$ ......(ii)

Dividing (ii) by (i), we get

$\dfrac{n + 2}{n} = \dfrac{260}{220} = \dfrac{13}{11}$

$11n + 22 = 13n$

$n = 11$

So, $11\dfrac{v}{4l} = 220$

$\dfrac{v}{4l} = 20$

So fundamental frequency is 20 Hz.

84969.subject: Zoology
84969.text: Differentiation of organs and tissues in a developing organism, is associated with:
84969.sol:
Differential expression of different genes at different stages of development leads to organ and tissues differentiation, for example, size and pattern of puffs of polytene chromosomes, which are site of transcription, varies at different developmental stages, indicating differential gene activity. Transcription factor is the molecular basis of organ differentiation.
Related Theory
The fate of a cell describes what it will become in the course of normal development. The fate of a particular cell can be discovered by labelling that cell and observing what structures it becomes a part of. The developmental potential, or potency, of a cell describes the range of different cell types it can become. The zygote and its very early descendants are totipotent - these cells have the potential to develop into a complete organism. The determination of different cell types (cell fates) involves progressive restrictions in their developmental potentials. Differentiation follows determination, as the cell elaborates a cell-specific developmental program. Differentiation results in the presence of cell types that have clear-cut identities, such as muscle cells, nerve cells, and skin cells.

85132.subject: Zoology
85132.text: A high density of elephant population in an area can result in:
85132.sol:
The intraspecific competition is competition between individuals of same species. The intraspecific competition may be very severe becauseall the members of a species have similar requirements of food, habitat mate, etc and they also have similar adaptations to gettheir needs. An interaction between individuals of different species wherein both are negatively affected is interspecific competition. An interaction between two species wherein both species involved are benefited is Mutualism. Predation is the act of preying on other animals is termed predation. The animal which hunts and kills other animals for food, is called the predator and the attacked animal is called the prey.
Related Theory
The principle of competitive exclusion was proposed by Gause states that two species competing for the same resources cannot coexist. One population will drive off the other one. If any of the members of the depleted population remains, that would be because they have adapted themselves according to the different niche.

85534.subject: Zoology
85534.text: Consider the following four statements (I-IV) related to the common frog Rana tigrina, and select the correct option stating which ones are true (T) and which ones are false $(\mathrm{F})$. I. On dry land it would die due to lack of $\mathrm{O}_2$ its mouth is forcibly kept closed for a few days. II. It has four-chambered heart. III. On day land it turns uricotelic from ureotelic. IV. Its life-history is carried out in pond water.
85534.sol:
Frogs respire on land and in the water by two different methods. In water, skin acts as aquatic respiratory organ (cutaneous respiration). Dissolved $\mathrm{O}_2$ in the water is exchanged through the skin by diffusion. On land, the buccal cavity, skin and lungs act as the respiratory organs. The respiration by lungs is called is called pulmonary respiration.
In frog, heart has three-chambers, two atria and one ventricle, and is covered by a membrane called pericardium.
The frog excretes urea and thus is a ureotelic animal. It never becomes uricotelic.
In frog, fertilization is external and takes place in water.

100025.subject: Physics
100025.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The random error in a measurement can be minimized by taking a large number of observations and finding their arithmetic mean.
Reason (R): Random errors occur irregularly and are equally likely to be positive or negative.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
100025.sol:
Random errors are those errors which occur irregularly and hence are random with respect to sign and size. They can be positive or negative. When a large number of observations are taken, the positive and negative random errors tend to cancel each other out. Therefore, the arithmetic mean of all observations is taken as the most accurate reading, which effectively minimizes the random error. Thus, both Assertion and Reason are correct, and the Reason correctly explains why taking the mean minimizes the error.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

100096.subject: Physics
100096.text: A theoretical model suggests that the power $P$ generated by a wind turbine depends on the blade length $L$, wind speed $v$, air density $\rho$, and the acceleration due to gravity $g$. If the relationship is given by $P \propto L^\alpha v^\beta \rho^\gamma g^\delta$, which of the following sets of exponents is dimensionally consistent?
100096.sol:
Write the dimensional formula for each physical quantity:
Power $P = [M L^2 T^{-3}]$
Length $L = [L]$
Velocity $v = [L T^{-1}]$
Density $\rho = [M L^{-3}]$
Acceleration due to gravity $g = [L T^{-2}]$

Using the principle of dimensional homogeneity:
$[M L^2 T^{-3}] = [L]^\alpha [L T^{-1}]^\beta [M L^{-3}]^\gamma [L T^{-2}]^\delta$
$[M L^2 T^{-3}] = [M^\gamma L^{\alpha + \beta - 3\gamma + \delta} T^{-\beta - 2\delta}]$

Equating the powers of $M$, $L$, and $T$ on both sides:
For $M$: $\gamma = 1$
For $T$: $-\beta - 2\delta = -3 \Rightarrow \beta + 2\delta = 3$
For $L$: $\alpha + \beta - 3\gamma + \delta = 2$

Substitute $\gamma = 1$ into the $L$ equation:
$\alpha + \beta - 3(1) + \delta = 2 \Rightarrow \alpha + \beta + \delta = 5$

Now check the given options to see which satisfies both $\beta + 2\delta = 3$ and $\alpha + \beta + \delta = 5$:
Option 4 gives $\alpha=2, \beta=3, \gamma=1, \delta=0$.
$\beta + 2\delta = 3 + 0 = 3$ (Satisfied)
$\alpha + \beta + \delta = 2 + 3 + 0 = 5$ (Satisfied)
Thus, this is the correct set of exponents.

Answer: $\alpha=2, \beta=3, \gamma=1, \delta=0$

101679.subject: Physics
101679.text: A small spherical ball of radius $r$ falls from rest in a long column of a viscous liquid. After it reaches terminal velocity, the rate of heat production due to viscous friction is proportional to $r^n$. The value of $n$ is:
101679.sol:
The rate of heat production is equal to the mechanical power dissipated by the viscous drag force.

Power $P = F \times v$, where $F$ is the viscous drag force and $v$ is the terminal velocity.

According to Stokes' law, the viscous drag force at terminal velocity is $F = 6\pi\eta r v$.

Therefore, the rate of heat production is:

$P = (6\pi\eta r v) \times v = 6\pi\eta r v^2$

The terminal velocity $v$ of a spherical ball of radius $r$ is given by:

$v = \dfrac{2r^2(\rho - \sigma)g}{9\eta}$

This shows that $v \propto r^2$.

Substituting $v \propto r^2$ into the power equation:

$P \propto r \times (r^2)^2$

$P \propto r \times r^4 = r^5$

Thus, the rate of heat production is proportional to $r^5$, which means $n = 5$.

Answer: $5$

103534.subject: Physics
103534.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If the uniform magnetic field in which a magnetic needle oscillates is increased by $300\%$, its time period becomes half of its initial value.
Reason (R): The time period of oscillation of a magnetic dipole is inversely proportional to the square root of the magnitude of the magnetic field.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
103534.sol:
The time period of oscillation of a magnetic dipole in a uniform magnetic field is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{I}{MB}}$.

From this formula, it is clear that $T \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{B}}$. Hence, the Reason (R) is true.

If the magnetic field is increased by $300\%$, the new magnetic field becomes:
$B' = B + \dfrac{300}{100}B = 4B$

The new time period $T'$ will be:
$T' \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{B'}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{4B}} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{B}}$

Therefore, $T' = \dfrac{T}{2}$. The time period becomes half of its initial value. Hence, the Assertion (A) is true.

Since the inverse square root relationship directly leads to the halving of the time period, the Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

According to Raoult's law and the properties of solutions:

(A) Carbon disulfide and acetone form a non-ideal solution showing a positive deviation from Raoult's law because the solute-solvent interactions are weaker than the solute-solute and solvent-solvent interactions.

(B) Phenol and aniline form a non-ideal solution showing a negative deviation from Raoult's law due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding between the phenolic proton and the lone pair on the nitrogen of aniline.

(C) n-Hexane and n-heptane have similar structures and intermolecular forces, forming an ideal solution.

(D) Ethanol and water (at approximately 95% by volume of ethanol) form a minimum boiling azeotrope, which is characteristic of solutions showing a large positive deviation from Raoult's law.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(iii), (B)-(ii), (C)-(i), (D)-(iv).

Answer: (A)-(iii), (B)-(ii), (C)-(i), (D)-(iv)

114910.text:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Slope of $\ln k$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T}$(I) $\log_{10} A$
(B) Intercept of $\ln k$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T}$(II) $-\dfrac{E_a}{2.303 R}$
(C) Slope of $\log_{10} k$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T}$(III) $\ln A$
(D) Intercept of $\log_{10} k$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T}$(IV) $-\dfrac{E_a}{R}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
114910.sol:
The Arrhenius equation is $k = A e^{-\dfrac{E_a}{RT}}$.

Taking the natural logarithm on both sides yields:
$\ln k = \ln A - \dfrac{E_a}{RT}$
Comparing this with the equation of a straight line $y = mx + c$, a plot of $\ln k$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T}$ has a slope of $-\dfrac{E_a}{R}$ and an intercept of $\ln A$.

Converting the equation to base 10 logarithm gives:
$2.303 \log_{10} k = 2.303 \log_{10} A - \dfrac{E_a}{RT}$
$\log_{10} k = \log_{10} A - \dfrac{E_a}{2.303 RT}$
Comparing this with $y = mx + c$, a plot of $\log_{10} k$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T}$ has a slope of $-\dfrac{E_a}{2.303 R}$ and an intercept of $\log_{10} A$.

Therefore, the correct matches are:
(A) Slope of $\ln k$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T} \rightarrow -\dfrac{E_a}{R}$ (IV)
(B) Intercept of $\ln k$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T} \rightarrow \ln A$ (III)
(C) Slope of $\log_{10} k$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T} \rightarrow -\dfrac{E_a}{2.303 R}$ (II)
(D) Intercept of $\log_{10} k$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T} \rightarrow \log_{10} A$ (I)

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

117090.subject: Chemistry
117090.text: Among the elements of the first transition series, zinc exhibits the lowest enthalpy of atomisation ($126 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$). What is the primary fundamental reason for this observation?
options: The high effective nuclear charge of zinc tightly binds its valence electrons.
The exceptional stability of its completely filled $4s$ orbital prevents metallic bonding.
The absence of unpaired electrons in its $3d$ subshell leads to weak interatomic metallic bonding.
The relatively larger atomic radius of zinc decreases the electrostatic attraction between atoms.
117090.sol:
The enthalpy of atomisation is a direct measure of the strength of interatomic metallic bonds in a solid lattice.

In transition metals, the strength of metallic bonding depends largely on the number of unpaired electrons available in the $(n-1)d$ subshell, which participate in bonding along with the $ns$ electrons.

Zinc has a ground state electronic configuration of $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{10} 4s^{2}$. Because its $3d$ subshell is completely filled, it possesses no unpaired $d$-electrons to contribute to the metallic bond.

This lack of unpaired $d$-electrons results in very weak interatomic metallic bonding, which is why zinc has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation in the $3d$ series.

Answer: The absence of unpaired electrons in its $3d$ subshell leads to weak interatomic metallic bonding.

117119.subject: Chemistry
117119.text: Which of the following ions has a 'spin only' magnetic moment of $3.87 \text{ BM}$?
117119.sol:
The spin-only magnetic moment ($\mu$) is given by the formula $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM}$, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

Given $\mu = 3.87 \text{ BM}$:
$\sqrt{n(n+2)} = 3.87$
$n(n+2) \approx 15$
This gives $n = 3$ unpaired electrons.

Now, let us check the electronic configuration of the given ions:
$\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ ($Z=28$): $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^8 \rightarrow 2$ unpaired electrons.
$\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ ($Z=26$): $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^6 \rightarrow 4$ unpaired electrons.
$\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$ ($Z=29$): $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^9 \rightarrow 1$ unpaired electron.
$\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$ ($Z=27$): $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^7 \rightarrow 3$ unpaired electrons.

Therefore, $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$ has $3$ unpaired electrons and a magnetic moment of $3.87 \text{ BM}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$
